page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition
lines: A system is the part of the universe chosen
The rest of the universe, which can exchange
matter or energy with it, is called the
surroundings. A boundary separates the two.
steps.why: Thermodynamics compares energy before and after a change, so it must first fix exactly which part of the universe is being watched. Naming the surroundings shows where the rest of the universe stands.
common_mistakes: Writing the universe instead of a part of the universe.
steps.memory_tip: System is the part under study. Surroundings is everything else.
steps.margin_note: The words part of the universe must appear.

steps.label: The example
lines: Example: for a reaction in a beaker, the
reaction mixture is the system; the beaker,
the air and everything else around it are

lines.text: System: the part of the universe chosen for study

steps.why: The question asks for an example, so a definition alone is incomplete. The printed model answer in the source book skips the example; write one anyway.
common_mistakes: Stopping after the definition. The example carries its own mark.
steps.memory_tip: Picture one beaker on a bench. Contents are the system; bench and room are the surroundings.
steps.margin_note: Any clear example is accepted: a gas in a cylinder, water in a flask, a reaction mixture.

insider_note: The question says give an example and the book's own model answer forgets it. Students who copy the book lose that mark.
